title: Recovery time and recovery point objectives
status_rationale: No production deployment, hosting provider, DR topology or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; RTO/RPO values in RR-UNB-RES-003-r2 are labeled candidates pending approval.
target_answer: Recovery objectives are defined per data class and per capability in one versioned table referenced by each contract: acknowledged authoritative financial and security commits (ledger, reservations, approvals, holds, payee versions, authority, payment intents) have RPO zero and RTO of four hours or less; issued documents RPO zero and RTO 24 hours; operational records RPO 15 minutes and RTO 24 hours; rebuildable projections are rebuilt rather than restored. The fault assumptions under which RPO zero holds are stated explicitly, and a tenant may buy stricter RTO with a matching isolation profile.
current_practice: Candidate values exist in RR-UNB-RES-003-r2; they are not approved and no infrastructure exists to meet them.
intended_practice: Approve objectives before architecture acceptance and verify by restore test before production use.
customer_statement: Our design targets zero data loss for acknowledged financial transactions and recovery within four hours for the financial core. These are candidate design targets; no production system exists and they have not been tested.

title: Failover, regional resilience and split-brain prevention
status_rationale: No production deployment, hosting provider, DR topology or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; RTO/RPO values in RR-UNB-RES-003-r2 are labeled candidates pending approval.
target_answer: Unbound runs one component monolith on managed PostgreSQL with quorum-durable synchronous replication across availability zones and a fenced single writer. Authoritative financial writes are suspended, not redirected, when safe quorum is lost, so availability is traded for correctness. Regional loss is handled by restore or promotion in a secondary region that honors the tenant's residency, with an RTO stated separately for regional events. Failback requires replica catch-up and reconciliation. Cloud-provider exit is addressed by portability of data and infrastructure definitions, not by active multi-cloud.
current_practice: Not established. REQ-X-006 and the resilience research note define the intended design.
intended_practice: Select provider and topology; implement fencing and quorum tests before payment features launch.
customer_statement: No production hosting has been selected. Our design suspends financial writes rather than risk inconsistent data during failover. Regional recovery objectives are not yet defined.

challenge.customer_intent: Keep the service running through a data center or region failure.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Extended outage, or worse, inconsistent financial state after failover.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Active-active multi-region designs maximize availability but introduce conflict resolution and split-brain risk for financial ledgers; vendors often report failover success without proving no transactions were lost or duplicated.
challenge.legally_required: No statute sets vendor topology. FFIEC guidance expects banks to understand vendor resilience; EU DORA requires EU financial entities to have ICT continuity arrangements and to contract for them.
challenge.contractually_required: Bank contracts often ask for geographically separated recovery sites.
challenge.historical_convention: Hot site or secondary data center expectations from core banking.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Split brain is eliminated in scope by a fenced single writer that refuses writes without quorum.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Fencing tokens and quorum checks enforced by the database and ledger component.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Fault-injection test results on each release.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Fail closed for money movement, fail open for read-only access, and prove it with fault injection.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by test results and exercise reports.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If the managed database cannot provide quorum-durable synchronous commit across zones.
challenge.alternative_risks: Regional RTO may be longer than a multi-region active design.
supporting_arguments: Correctness of money is the customer's primary concern.
A single-writer design is simpler to test exhaustively.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain: customers may read 'suspends writes' as lower availability.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Customers comparing headline uptime may prefer active-active vendors.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: DR testing and evidence
status_rationale: No production deployment, hosting provider, DR topology or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; RTO/RPO values in RR-UNB-RES-003-r2 are labeled candidates pending approval.
target_answer: Every data class is restored at least annually per isolation profile, and failover is exercised at least annually, with measured RTO and RPO compared to objectives. A fault-injection suite runs on each release in a production-like environment. Evidence is generated automatically, time-stamped and digest-protected, and test evidence is labeled distinct from production evidence. Customers receive exercise summaries under NDA.
current_practice: Not established. SOC2-015 and RR-UNB-RES-003-r2 require dated recovery test evidence.
intended_practice: Run first restore and failover exercises in a pre-production environment before production launch.
customer_statement: No disaster recovery test has been performed because no production environment exists. We plan annual exercises with measured results shared under NDA.

title: Recovery dependency mapping and clean rebuild
status_rationale: No production deployment, hosting provider, DR topology or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; RTO/RPO values in RR-UNB-RES-003-r2 are labeled candidates pending approval.
target_answer: A generated dependency map shows what each capability needs to recover and in which order, including DNS, identity provider, key management, secrets, CI/CD and payment connectivity. The whole environment can be rebuilt from source, infrastructure definitions and Strata-managed schema into a clean account, which is the recovery path for destructive cyber events such as ransomware or cloud-account compromise. Encryption keys have documented recovery procedures so that key loss cannot make backups unreadable.
current_practice: Not established. Strata exists as a declarative schema tool in pilot status (PostgreSQL 16 only) but is not operated for any production Echelon service.
intended_practice: Adopt infrastructure as code from the first environment; test clean rebuild twice a year.
provable: Strata can compile and diff schemas today; no environment rebuild has been performed.
customer_statement: We intend to be able to rebuild the full environment from source into a clean account. This is a design intent and has not been tested.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Tenant-level restoration
status_rationale: No production deployment, hosting provider, DR topology or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; RTO/RPO values in RR-UNB-RES-003-r2 are labeled candidates pending approval.
target_answer: A single tenant can be restored to a chosen point in time without affecting other tenants, using tooling bound to one verified tenant context and verified by negative isolation tests. The capability depends on isolation profile: dedicated databases restore independently; shared physical backups do not by themselves guarantee independent tenant recovery, and Echelon discloses that limit. Tenants on dedicated profiles may have separately configured and tested objectives.
current_practice: Not established. UNB-TEN-014 explicitly warns that shared physical backups do not guarantee tenant-selective recovery.
intended_practice: Default to dedicated database per tenant (Profile B) and test tenant-selective restore annually.
customer_statement: Our design isolates each sponsor in its own database by default so it can be restored independently. This has not been built or tested.

challenge.customer_intent: Recover our data after our own error or a corruption without waiting for, or harming, other customers.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Restore of a shared database rolls back other tenants or exposes their data.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Most multi-tenant vendors restore whole databases and extract one tenant manually, which is slow and error-prone.
challenge.historical_convention: Single-tenant hosting made this trivial; SaaS made it rare.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Per-tenant databases eliminate cross-tenant rollback in scope.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Restore tooling accepts exactly one tenant context.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Per-tenant database plus append-only history allows both restore and deterministic replay to a point.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If cost pressure forces shared-schema Profile A for small tenants.
challenge.alternative_risks: More databases increase operational overhead and upgrade coordination.
supporting_arguments: agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Per-tenant databases cost more at small scale.

title: Financial integrity and payment safety after recovery
status_rationale: No production deployment, hosting provider, DR topology or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; RTO/RPO values in RR-UNB-RES-003-r2 are labeled candidates pending approval.
target_answer: After any restore or failover, payment release stays blocked until consistency checks across all C0 stores pass and external bank and custodian outcomes are reconciled; payments with Unknown outcomes cannot be re-sent until resolved through the rail's protocol. Protective holds and cancellations are replayed before anything else, and independent authorization is required to lift the lock. If a recovery would lose an acknowledged financial fact, an approved procedure defines compensating records and customer notice.
current_practice: Not established. REQ-X-006, RR-REQ-X-004-r1 and RR-UNB-RES-003-r2 specify this behavior; the acceptance scenario in REQ-X-006 is marked not executed.
intended_practice: Implement the release lock and reconciliation gate as part of the payments component; include in every restore exercise.
customer_statement: Our design keeps payments blocked after any recovery until balances and payment outcomes are reconciled, to prevent duplicate or lost payments. This has not been built or tested.

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure recovery does not create financial errors.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Payments resent after restore, holds lost, canceled grants paid.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional DR questions measure time to restore and ignore whether restored state is safe to act on; a fast restore that replays stale instructions is worse than a slow one.
challenge.legally_required: No specific rule for Echelon; Nacha and UCC 4A allocate loss for erroneous payments to the originator and its bank, which is the customer.
challenge.historical_convention: Core processors reconcile after recovery by manual procedure.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Duplicate dispatch is eliminated in scope by an idempotent payment chain that blocks re-dispatch while an outcome is Unknown.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Release lock is a typed state the dispatch path cannot bypass.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Treat RTO for money movement as time to safe, reconciled state, and report it that way.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If provider reconciliation data is unavailable for long periods.
challenge.alternative_risks: Payments may stay blocked longer than the customer tolerates.
supporting_arguments: Prevents the most damaging recovery error.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely for finance teams; uncertain for buyers who compare headline RTO.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Disaster declaration, communication and customer responsibilities
status_rationale: No production deployment, hosting provider, DR topology or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; RTO/RPO values in RR-UNB-RES-003-r2 are labeled candidates pending approval.
target_answer: Named roles may declare a disaster; customers are notified through pre-registered alternate channels within one hour of declaration, receive status at defined intervals, and receive a post-event report within ten business days stating achieved RTO and RPO against commitments. Complementary customer responsibilities (verifying balances, resubmitting rejected requests, confirming out-of-band payments) are documented in advance.
intended_practice: Define declaration authority and notification procedure with the continuity plan.
customer_statement: We have not yet defined disaster declaration authority or notification timelines. We plan to document them, including customer responsibilities, before production.
